introduction: Managers today are expected to work with data themselves, not wait for someone else to do it. This hands-on workshop teaches students to take raw business data, clean it, analyse it and turn it into a decision. Building on Digital Productivity Tools (BBA106) and Business Statistics (BBA204), students work first in Excel and then in Python (Jupyter), using the same business datasets in both so they learn when each tool is the better choice. Every session is built around practice in the lab. The course ends with a final showcase, where teams present a data-based recommendation to a jury. It prepares students for Research Methodology (BBA402) and the Business Analytics specialisation.
plagiarism: Plagiarism above 15% (checked by software) in any submission, or any use of unauthorised AI tools in exams, leads to zero marks for that component. Repeat cases go to the Academic Integrity Committee, chaired by the Dean.

objectives.text: To build confidence in preparing and summarising business data in Excel and Python.
To introduce regression and forecasting as practical tools for business decisions.
To develop the habit of questioning data, methods and results before acting on them.
To develop the ability to explain analysis clearly to a non-technical business audience.

McKinney, Wes. Python for Data Analysis. O'Reilly Media. (latest edition; to be confirmed by faculty)

clos.text: Clean, summarise and visualise business data using Excel and Python.
clos.plg_label: PLG 1: Understanding and Application of Fundamentals
clos.mode: Studio and Lab Exercises: Excel and Python lab submissions
clos.exceed: Prepares data accurately with no prompting, chooses the most suitable summaries and charts, and writes clean, reusable work in both tools.
clos.meet: Prepares data with minor errors and produces correct summaries and charts in both tools.
clos.below: Leaves major data errors unresolved, or produces summaries and charts that are wrong or misleading.
clos.analysis: 80.0% of students met or exceeded expectations against a target of 70%, and 20.0% did not meet them. The class averaged 63.7% on this CLO. It was assessed through Excel and Python Labs.
clos.improvement: Add a revision session on Excel and Python Labs before the assessment.

clos.text: Identify a business problem and use regression or forecasting techniques to suggest a data-based solution.
clos.mode: Studio and Lab Exercises: regression and forecasting lab submissions
clos.exceed: Frames the problem precisely, selects and tests a suitable model, compares alternatives, and proposes a well-justified solution.
clos.meet: Frames the problem clearly, applies a suitable model correctly, and proposes a solution consistent with the results.
clos.below: Frames the problem poorly, applies an unsuitable model, or proposes a solution the results do not support.
clos.analysis: 72.5% of students met or exceeded expectations against a target of 70%, and 27.5% did not meet them. The class averaged 60.1% on this CLO. It was assessed through Regression and Forecasting Labs.
clos.improvement: Add one more practice case on Regression and Forecasting Labs, and share two sample answers at different rubric levels.

clos.text: Critically evaluate analytical results, their limits and their impact across business functions.
clos.mode: Final Showcase: evaluation of results and limitations (peer review as a supporting measure)
clos.exceed: Tests the results for weaknesses, explains the limits of the data, and traces the impact across several business functions.
clos.meet: Notes the main limits of the analysis and links the results to the relevant business functions.
clos.below: Accepts the results without question, or does not link them to the wider business.
clos.analysis: 60.0% of students met or exceeded expectations against a target of 70%, and 40.0% did not meet them. The class averaged 50.3% on this CLO. It was assessed through Showcase Evaluation.
clos.improvement: Add two graded practice cases on Showcase Evaluation before the assessment, with a worked model answer and the rubric shared in advance.

clos.text: Present a data-based recommendation clearly to a business audience.
clos.mode: Final Showcase: team presentation to a jury
clos.exceed: Leads with the recommendation, tells a clear story with well-chosen visuals, and answers jury questions with confidence.
clos.meet: States the recommendation clearly, uses readable visuals, and answers most jury questions.
clos.below: The recommendation is unclear, visuals are hard to follow, or the team cannot answer basic questions.
clos.analysis: 95.0% of students met or exceeded expectations against a target of 70%, and 5.0% did not meet them. The class averaged 67.4% on this CLO. It was assessed through Showcase Presentation.
clos.improvement: Keep the current approach, and raise the Bloom's level of Showcase Presentation so the CLO is tested in more depth.

sessions.topic: Introduction to business analytics: types of business data, the analytics process, setting up Excel and Jupyter
sessions.reading: Albright and Winston: introduction to business analytics

sessions.topic: Excel for analysis: cleaning data, lookups, pivot tables, summary statistics, dashboards
Python for analysis: Python basics, loading, cleaning and summarising data with pandas
Data visualisation in Excel and Python: choosing the right chart, avoiding misleading charts
Regression and forecasting: simple and multiple regression, trend and seasonality, testing a forecast
sessions.reading: Albright and Winston: regression; time series

sessions.topic: Analytics across business functions: marketing, finance and operations examples, limits of analysis, data privacy
Showcase clinic: team analysis review and peer review
Final showcase: team presentations to a jury
